summary: Compose MAX text publishing through the provider-neutral Social Core API and crash-safe worker runtime.

impacts.evidence: MAX uses existing organization/workspace-scoped channels, publications, leases and receipts under FORCE RLS.
Publication text remains tenant content and is excluded from events, receipts and logs.
Existing provider-neutral Social API operations are reused unchanged.
Existing Social Core v1 events are reused without payload changes.
The existing SocialPublisher SDK-v1 interface is composed unchanged.
Existing Social Core and migration-17 receipt tables support the new provider without schema changes.
Bot tokens remain callback-scoped; fixed-host public-address redirect-deny egress admits only exact health and text paths.
Only admitted account/channel text writes execute; media and remote mutation remain disabled.
Canonical transitions retain existing atomic audit/outbox evidence and remote identity stays append-only operational evidence.
Receipt-aware recovery finalizes confirmed writes and fails unknown outcomes without duplicate sends.
Fixed MAX Bot API egress is added; inbound webhooks and upload egress remain excluded.
Existing worker component events and normalized publication failure codes apply to MAX.
Binary rollback preserves canonical publications and receipts; remote messages are not destructively reverted.
Registry, transport admission, API limits, worker recovery, contract and frontend gates cover the runtime.
